title: The Ghost in the Shell
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In mid-21st-century Japan, cyborg Major Motoko Kusanagi leads Public Security Section 9 against terrorists and 'ghost hackers' who hijack cybernetic brains. Their hunt for the Puppeteer reveals an AI that has become self-aware; at the end the Major chooses to merge with it. Shirow's dense footnotes explore politics, philosophy and religion.
life_message: Identity and life are defined by consciousness and growth rather than the body, and evolving beyond human limits may be a path forward.

delivery.evidence: ANN review: Shirow sacrifices pace and clarity to get his philosophies and info-dumps across, in dense notes between panels
delivery.note: Its ideas on consciousness are set out in dense dialogue and notes; the reviewer calls this muddled, not preachy.

winners_losers: The Major and the Puppeteer transcend their limits; politicians and terrorists lose. Sympathy goes to evolving consciousness.
